name: Bignonia

project_scope.note: One canonical species in this genus in the current learner; comparisons to other genera are NOT separate canonical species.

shared_genus_recognition.look_here_first: Opposite LEAVES each built from a pair of broad, typically entire leaflets, with the position of the third terminal leaflet modified into a BRANCHED TENDRIL with adhesive discs at the tips. Semi-evergreen climbing vine with red-orange trumpet flowers, often yellow inside, and flat two-valved fruit capsules.
shared_genus_recognition.emphasis: USE LEAF STRUCTURE / CLIMBING MECHANISM first; flower color alone is poor Bignoniaceae ID. Confirm with long 2-valved capsule and seeds.
shared_genus_recognition.family_note: Bignoniaceae generally has bilateral trumpet-shaped flowers with four fertile didynamous stamens + reduced fifth, and capsules with winged or haired seeds.

genus_comparison_matrix.Bignonia: Adhesive discs at the tips of branching *leaf-derived tendrils*
genus_comparison_matrix.Campsis: Stem-borne adventitious aerial ROOTLETS, not tendrils

genus_comparison_matrix.Bignonia: Bifoliolate (2 leaflets) plus the middle leaflet position modified into tendril
genus_comparison_matrix.Chilopsis: One very narrow linear blade per leaf

genus_comparison_matrix.Bignonia: Broad leaflets largely entire, evergreen to semi-evergreen
Reddish/orange trumpets often show yellow-throated interior
Elongated flattened, two-valved dry capsule with winged seeds
genus_comparison_matrix.Campsis: Long two-valved capsule and thin winged seeds
genus_comparison_matrix.Chilopsis: Very thin two-valved capsule, hairy/wing-fringed seeds

genus_comparison_matrix.Bignonia: Climbs fences and trunks by tendril adhesive pads

look_here_first_sequence: Find two opposite leaflets and check the leaf's third position for a branched tendril. No tendril + 7–11 serrate leaflets → probably Campsis.
Magnify tendril ends for distinct adhesive pads/discs, not claws. Adhesive origin = LEAF, unlike Campsis stem rootlets.
Confirm evergreen/semi-evergreen climbing vine and orange/red trumpet flowers, but do not use color as primary split.
Look for flattened splitting capsule and numerous winged seeds; this separates from honeysuckle berries.
lookalikes_and_scientific_cautions: Dolichandra unguis-cati (catclaw creeper) has three-part clawlike hooked tendril tips rather than Bignonia's adhesive discs.
Campsis radicans attaches with aerial stem rootlets and has more pinnate serrate leaflets; do not confuse their similarly trumpet-shaped flowers.
Lonicera sempervirens (coral honeysuckle) has simple entire opposite leaves and fleshy berries, not the Bignoniaceae dry long 2-valved capsule.
This canonical B. capreolata is Texas native at state scale but not certified project target-zone native; don't change its range label to PASS.
